sector_notes: As of the latest completed US session on October 23, the Energy Select Sector ETF (XLE) rose 2.60% to $69.33 and closed near its reported 52-week high of $69.72. The broad tape weakened into the close: SPY fell about 1.2% from October 20 to October 23, QQQ fell about 1.8%, and semiconductor ETF SMH declined about 3.5%, indicating that leadership is selective rather than a broad technology advance. Brent crude traded near $114.61 early October 26 versus a Friday close near $117.21, easing slightly while remaining elevated; Reuters reports US futures little changed ahead of a heavy earnings week and an expected Federal Reserve hold on Wednesday. Software and cybersecurity are bifurcated: CRWD, PANW, NET, DDOG and FTNT remain above their 50-day and 200-day averages, while investors are increasingly focused on whether hyperscaler AI capital spending can generate sufficient returns.
